analysis:
Integration review of the SSD complete-checkpoint startup scan change. In provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift (scanOnDisk, removeCorrupt), removeCorrupt is split into a private removeFile(tag) and a counter increment. removeFile keeps the same performIndexedRemoval, removeItemIfSafe and index.remove path. The TTL check moves out of the validation guard into its own guard, so a TTL-expired file now calls removeFile and continues without being indexed. All other validation failures (header, metadata, blockSize, lookupTag prefix, missing attributes) still go through removeCorrupt, which deletes the file and counts it.

T-041 effects: the 30-minute TTL at startup is still enforced (expired files unlinked, never indexed). HMAC lookup names, DBK3 AES-GCM, AAD, the TTL value, KEK-wipe purge and account/salt scoping are untouched. Per-file removal still does not rotate the epoch, consistent with the T-041 detection_hint. The only behavioral difference is telemetry: corrupt_drops_total no longer includes expiries. The new test (SSDHybridCheckpointRecencyTests) asserts that real corruption (3 garbage bytes) is still counted and deleted, and that expiry is not counted. Changelog and docs (ssd-kv-cache.md lines 88-91) match the code.

Remaining limits: unchanged parts of scanOnDisk and any consumers of corruptDropped outside the supplied evidence were not seen. A tampered mtime can already cause a file to be treated as unexpired or expired, and the T-041 text notes that TTL is not an anti-rollback proof. This change does not worsen that. No regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption identified.
